questions.q: Number of integral terms in the expansion of ${\left\{{7}^{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} + {11}^{\left(\dfrac{1}{6}\right)}\right\}}^{824}$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
We know that,

General term in expansion of ${\left(( 7{)}^{1 / 2} + ( 11{)}^{1 / 6}\right)}^{824}$ is given by,

${t}_{r + 1} = Cr 824 \cdot 7\dfrac{824 - r}{2} \cdot 11\dfrac{r}{6}$

For integral term, $r$ must be multiple of $6$ and should be less than $824$

So, the series will be $r = 0, 6, 12, . . . . . 822$

Now, finding number of terms we get,

$822 = 0 + \left(n - 1\right)6$

$⇒ 137 = \left(n - 1\right)$

$⇒ n = 138$

Hence, total integral terms will be $138$

questions.solution:
Given expansion is ${\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{2{x}^{\dfrac{2}{3}}}\right)}^{18}$.

$⇒ {T}_{7} = C6 18 {\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{12}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2{x}^{\dfrac{2}{3}}}\right)}^{6}$

$⇒ m = C6 18 {\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{12}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{6}$

$⇒ {T}_{13} = C12 18 {\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{6}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2{x}^{\dfrac{2}{3}}}\right)}^{12}$

$⇒ n = C12 18 {\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{6}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{12}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m}{n} = \dfrac{C6 18 {\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{12}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{6}}{C12 18 {\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{6}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{12}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m}{n} = \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{6}}{{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{6}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m}{n} = {\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)}^{6}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{m}{n}\right)\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{4}{9}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{9}{4}$

questions.q: In the expansion of $\left(1 + x\right)\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right){\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{x} + \dfrac{3}{{x}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}\right)}^{5}, x \ne 0$, the sum of the coefficient of ${x}^{3}$ and ${x}^{- 13}$ is equal to ______
questions.solution:
Given,

$\left(1 + x\right)\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right){\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{x} + \dfrac{3}{{x}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}}\right)}^{5}$

$= {\left(1 + x\right)}^{2}\left(1 - x\right){\left(\dfrac{{x}^{3} + 3{x}^{2} + 3x + 1}{{x}^{3}}\right)}^{5}$

$= {\left(1 + x\right)}^{2}\left(1 - x\right){\left(\dfrac{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}\right)}^{5}$

$= \dfrac{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{17}\left(1 - x\right)}{{x}^{15}}$

$= \dfrac{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{17}}{{x}^{15}} - \dfrac{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{17}}{{x}^{14}}$

Now for coefficient of ${x}^{3}$, we will find coefficient of ${x}^{18}$ in expansion of ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{17}$ which is not possible and ${x}^{17}$ in expansion of $- {\left(1 + x\right)}^{17}$ which will be $- C17 17 = - 1$

And for coefficient of ${x}^{- 13}$ we will coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ in expansion of ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{17}$ which will be $C2 17$ and coefficient of $x$ in expansion of $- {\left(1 + x\right)}^{17}$ which will be $- C1 17$, so the coefficient of ${x}^{- 13}$ will be $C2 17 - C1 17 = 136 - 17 = 119$

Hence, the sum will be $119 - 1 = 118$

questions.q: If the coefficient of ${x}^{30}$ in the expansion of ${\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)}^{6}{\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)}^{7}{\left(1 - {x}^{3}\right)}^{8}; x \ne 0$ is $\alpha$, then $\left|\alpha\right|$ equals _________.
questions.solution:
Given expansion is ${\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)}^{6}{\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)}^{7}{\left(1 - {x}^{3}\right)}^{8}$.

Now, coefficient of ${x}^{30}$ in $\dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{6}{\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)}^{7}{\left(1 - {x}^{3}\right)}^{8}}{{x}^{6}}$

So, we will find the coefficient of ${x}^{36}$ in ${\left(1 + x\right)}^{6}{\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)}^{7}{\left(1 - {x}^{3}\right)}^{8}$

General term of the given expansion is${}^{6}{{C}_{{r}_{1}}}^{7}{{C}_{{r}_{2}}}^{8}{C}_{{r}_{3}}{\left(- 1\right)}^{{r}_{3}}{x}^{{r}_{1} + 2{r}_{2} + 3{r}_{3}}$.

$⇒ {r}_{1} + 2{r}_{2} + 3{r}_{3} = 36$

Case-I:

${r}_{1}$ ${r}_{2}$ ${r}_{3}$
$0$ $6$ $8$
$2$ $5$ $8$
$4$ $4$ $8$
$6$ $3$ $8$

$⇒ {r}_{1} + 2{r}_{2} = 12$ (Taking ${r}_{3} = 8$)

Case II:

${r}_{1}$ ${r}_{2}$ ${r}_{3}$
$1$ $7$ $7$
$3$ $6$ $7$
$5$ $5$ $7$

$⇒ {r}_{1} + 2{r}_{2} = 15$ (Taking ${r}_{3} = 7$)

Case III:

${r}_{1}$ ${r}_{2}$ ${r}_{3}$
$4$ $7$ $6$
$6$ $6$ $6$

$⇒ {r}_{1} + 2{r}_{2} = 18$ (Taking ${r}_{3} = 6$)

So, the required coefficient Is given by, $\alpha = 7 + \left(15 \times 21\right) + \left(15 \times 35\right) + \left(35\right) - \left(6 \times 8\right) - \left(20 \times 7 \times 8\right) - \left(6 \times 21 \times 8\right) + \left(15 \times 28\right) + \left(7 \times 28\right)$

$⇒ \alpha = - 678$

$⇒ \left|\alpha\right| = 678$

questions.q: Remainder when ${64}^{{32}^{32}}$ is divided by $9$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
Given,

${64}^{{32}^{32}} = {\left(63 + 1\right)}^{32 \times 32 \times 32 . . . . 32\text{times}}$

$⇒ {64}^{{32}^{32}} = {\left(63 + 1\right)}^{32\lambda}$

Now we know that by binomial theorem,

${\left(1 + 63\right)}^{32\lambda} = C0 {}^{32\lambda} \cdot 1 + C1 {}^{32\lambda} \cdot 1 \cdot 63 + C2 {}^{32\lambda} \cdot 1 \cdot {63}^{2} + . . . . . . .$

$⇒ {\left(1 + 63\right)}^{32\lambda} = 1 + 9\alpha$

So, when ${64}^{{32}^{32}}$ is divided by $9$ we get $1$ as remainder.

questions.q: $Cr n - 1 = \left({k}^{2} - 8\right) Cr + 1 n$ if and only if :
questions.solution:
Given: $Cr n - 1 = \left({k}^{2} - 8\right) Cr + 1 n . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ \mathop{\mathop{r + 1 \ge 0, r \ge 0}_{⏟}}_{r \ge 0}$

$⇒ \dfrac{Cr n - 1}{Cr + 1 n} = {k}^{2} - 8$

$⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{\left(n - 1\right) !}{r ! \left(n - r - 1\right) !}}{\dfrac{n !}{\left(r + 1\right) ! \left(n - r - 1\right) !}} = {k}^{2} - 8$

$⇒ \dfrac{r + 1}{n} = {k}^{2} - 8$

$⇒ {k}^{2} - 8 > 0$

$⇒ ( k - 2\sqrt{2} ) ( k + 2\sqrt{2} ) > 0$

$⇒ k \in ( - \infty , - 2\sqrt{2} ) ∪ ( 2\sqrt{2}, \infty ) . . . ( ii )$

Using equation $\left(i\right)$,

$⇒ n \ge r + 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{r + 1}{n} \le 1$

$⇒ {k}^{2} - 8 \le 1$

$⇒ {k}^{2} - 9 \le 0$

$⇒ - 3 \le k \le 3 . . . ( ii )$

From equation $\left(ii\right)\text{and}\left(iii\right)$ we get,

$k \in [ - 3, - 2\sqrt{2} ) ∪ ( 2\sqrt{2}, 3 ]$

questions.solution:
Given: $z = 2 - i\left(2tan\dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right)$

$⇒ z = 2\left[1 - itan\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right)\right]$

$⇒ z = 2\left[1 - \dfrac{isin\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right)}{cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right)}\right]$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{2}{cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right)}\left[cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right) - isin\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right)\right]$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{2}{cos\left(\pi - \dfrac{3\pi}{8}\right)}\left[cos\left(\pi - \dfrac{3\pi}{8}\right) - isin\left(\pi - \dfrac{3\pi}{8}\right)\right]$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{2}{- cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8}\right)}\left[- cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8}\right) - isin\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8}\right)\right]$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{2}{cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8}\right)}\left[cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8}\right) + isin\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8}\right)\right]$

$⇒ z = 2sec\dfrac{3\pi}{8}{e}^{i \cdot \dfrac{3\pi}{8}}$

Now on comparing with $z = \left|z\right|{e}^{i\theta}$ we get,

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{8}, r = 2sec\dfrac{3\pi}{8}$

questions.q: Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation ${x}^{2} - \sqrt{6}x + 3 = 0$ such that $Im ( \alpha ) > Im ( \beta )$. Let $a, b$ be integers not divisible by $3$and $n$ be a natural number such that $\dfrac{{\alpha}^{99}}{\beta} + {\alpha}^{98} = {3}^{n} ( a + ib ) , i = \sqrt{- 1}$. Then $n + a + b$ is equal to ___________.
questions.solution:
Given,

${x}^{2} - \sqrt{6}x + 3 = 0$ has roots $\alpha \text{ and } \beta$

Now, solving ${x}^{2} - \sqrt{6}x + 3 = 0$ we get,

$x = \dfrac{\sqrt{6} \pm i\sqrt{6}}{2} = \sqrt{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}i\right)$

Now, taking $\alpha = \sqrt{3}\left({e}^{i\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\right), \beta = \sqrt{3}\left({e}^{- i\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\right)$

Now, solving $\dfrac{{\alpha}^{99}}{\beta} + {\alpha}^{98} = {\alpha}^{98}\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta} + 1\right)$

$= \dfrac{{\alpha}^{98} ( \alpha + \beta )}{\beta}$

$= \dfrac{{3}^{49}{\left({e}^{i\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\right)}^{98}\left(\sqrt{6}\right)}{\sqrt{3}\left({e}^{- i\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\right)}$

$= {3}^{49}\left({e}^{i99\dfrac{\pi}{4}}\right) \times \sqrt{2}$

$= {3}^{49}\left(cos\dfrac{99\pi}{4} + isin\dfrac{99\pi}{4}\right) \times \sqrt{2}$

$= {3}^{49}\left(cos\left(25\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + isin\left(25\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right) \times \sqrt{2}$

$= {3}^{49} ( - 1 + i )$

$= {3}^{n} ( a + ib )$

So, on comparing we get,

$n = 49, a = - 1, b = 1$

$∴ n + a + b = 49 - 1 + 1 = 49$

questions.q: Let $P = \left\{z \in \mathbb{C}: \left|z + 2 - 3i\right| \le 1\right\}$ and $Q = \left\{z \in \mathbb{C}: z\left(1 + i\right) + \overset{¯}{z}\left(1 - i\right) \le - 8\right\}$. Let in $P ∩ Q, \left|z - 3 + 2i\right|$ be maximum and minimum at ${z}_{1}$ and ${z}_{2}$ respectively. If ${\left|{z}_{1}\right|}^{2} + 2{\left|z\right|}^{2} = \alpha + \beta\sqrt{2},$ where $\alpha, \beta$ are integers, then $\alpha + \beta$ equals __________
questions.solution:
Given: $\left|z + 2 - 3i\right| \le 1$

Putting, $z = x + iy$.

$⇒ {\left(x + 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 3\right)}^{2} \le 1 . . . \left(i\right)$

For the circle represented in equation $\left(i\right)$, centre is $\left(- 2, 3\right)$ and radius, $r = 1$.

It is given that, $z\left(1 + i\right) + z \left(1 - i\right) \le - 8$

$⇒ \left(x + iy\right)\left(1 + i\right) + \left(x - iy\right)\left(1 - i\right) \le - 8$

$⇒ x + ix - y + iy + x - ix - iy - y \le - 8$

$⇒ 2x - 2y \le - 8$

$⇒ x - y + 4 = 0$

So, the line passing through $\left(3, - 2\right)$ and perpendicular to $x - y + 4 = 0$ is given by, $x + y - 1 = 0$.

So, the distance of line $x - y + 4 = 0$ from the centre $\left(- 2, 3\right)$ is given by,

$d = \left|\dfrac{- 2 - 3 + 4}{\sqrt{2}}\right|$

$⇒ d = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Now, $x + y - 1 = 0$ can be rewritten as,

$\dfrac{x + 2}{\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}} = \dfrac{y - 3}{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} = CA\text{or}CB$

For $CA = \dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $CB = 1$, $A ≡ \left(\dfrac{- 3}{2}, \dfrac{5}{2}\right)$ and $B ≡ \left(\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}} - 2, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 3\right)$.

$⇒ {\left|{z}_{1}\right|}^{2} = {\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}^{2} + {\left(3 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left|{z}_{1}\right|}^{2} = 4 + \dfrac{1}{2} + 2\sqrt{2} + 9 + \dfrac{1}{2} + 3\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ {\left|{z}_{1}\right|}^{2} = 14 + 5\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ {\left|{z}_{2}\right|}^{2} = 2\left(\dfrac{9}{4} + \dfrac{25}{4}\right)$

$⇒ {\left|{z}_{2}\right|}^{2} = 17$

$⇒ {\left|{z}_{1}\right|}^{2} + 2{\left|{z}_{2}\right|}^{2} = 31 + 5\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \alpha = 31, \beta = 5$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta = 36$

questions.q: If $\alpha$ denotes the number of solutions of ${\left|1 - i\right|}^{x} = {2}^{x}$ and $\beta = \left(\dfrac{\left|z\right|}{arg\left(z\right)}\right)$, where $z = \dfrac{\pi}{4}{\left(1 + i\right)}^{4}\left(\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{\pi} \cdot i}{\sqrt{\pi} + i} + \dfrac{\sqrt{\pi} - i}{1 + \sqrt{\pi} \cdot i}\right)$, $i = \sqrt{- 1}$, then the distance of the point $\left(\alpha, \beta\right)$ from the line $4x - 3y = 7$ is ______
questions.solution:
Given,

${\left|1 - i\right|}^{x} = {2}^{x}$

$⇒ {\left(\sqrt{2}\right)}^{x} = {2}^{x}$

$⇒ x = 0$

Hence, the number of solutions will be one, so $\alpha = 1$

Now, solving

$z = \dfrac{\pi}{4}{\left(1 + i\right)}^{4}\left(\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{\pi} \cdot i}{\sqrt{\pi} + i} + \dfrac{\sqrt{\pi} - i}{1 + \sqrt{\pi} \cdot i}\right)$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{\pi}{4}{\left(1 + i\right)}^{4}\left[\dfrac{\sqrt{\pi} - \pii - i - \sqrt{\pi}}{\pi + 1} + \dfrac{\sqrt{\pi} - i - \pii - \sqrt{\pi}}{1 + \pi}\right]$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{\pi}{4}{\left(1 + i\right)}^{4}\left[\dfrac{- 2\pii - 2i}{\pi + 1}\right]$

$⇒ z = \dfrac{\pii}{2}{\left(1 + i\right)}^{4}$

$⇒ z = - \dfrac{\pii}{2}\left(1 + 4i + 6{i}^{2} + 4{i}^{3} + 1\right)$

$⇒ z = 2\pii$

So, $arg\left(z\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$⇒ \beta = \dfrac{\left|z\right|}{arg\left(z\right)} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\dfrac{\pi}{2}} = 4$

Hence, the distance from $\left(\alpha, \beta\right) ≡ \left(1, 4\right)$ to $4x - 3y = 7$ will be $\left|\dfrac{4 - 3 \times 4 - 7}{\sqrt{{4}^{2} + {3}^{2}}}\right| = \dfrac{15}{5} = 3$

questions.q: Let  $S = \left\{z \in C: \left|z - 1\right| = 1and\left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)\left(z + \overset{¯}{z}\right) - i\left(z - \overset{¯}{z}\right) = 2\sqrt{2}\right\}$. Let ${z}_{1}, {z}_{2} \in S$ be such that  $\left|{z}_{1}\right| = \mathop{max}_{z \in s}\left|z\right|$ and $\left|{z}_{2}\right| = \mathop{min}_{z \in s}\left|z\right|$. Then ${\left|\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|}^{2}$ equals:
questions.solution:
Given,

$\left|z - 1\right| = 1$

Now, let $z = x + iy$

$⇒ {\left(x - 1\right)}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 1 . . . \left(i\right)$

And 

$\left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)\left(z + \overset{¯}{z}\right) - i\left(z - \overset{¯}{z}\right) = 2\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)\left(2x\right) - i\left(2iy\right) = 2\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)x + y = \sqrt{2} . . . \left(ii\right)$

Solving $\left(i\right)\text{and}\left(ii\right)$,

$⇒ {\left(x - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left[\sqrt{2} - \left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)x\right]}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + 1 - 2x + 2 + {\left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)}^{2}{x}^{2} - 2\sqrt{2}\left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right)x = 1$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + 1 - 2x + 2 + \left(2 + 1 - 2\sqrt{2}\right){x}^{2} - 4x + 2\sqrt{2}x = 1$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - 2x + 2 + 3{x}^{2} - 2{x}^{2}\sqrt{2} - 4x + 2\sqrt{2}x = 0$

$⇒ 4{x}^{2} - 2{x}^{2}\sqrt{2} - 6x + 2\sqrt{2}x + 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(4 - 2\sqrt{2}\right){x}^{2} + \left(- 6 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)x + 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(4 - 2\sqrt{2}\right){x}^{2} + \left(- 4 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)x - 2x + 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(4 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)x\left(x - 1\right) - 2\left(x - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right)\left(\left(4 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)x - 2\right) = 0$

Either $x = 1$ or $x = \dfrac{1}{2 - \sqrt{2}} . . . \left(iii\right)$

On solving $\left(ii\right)\text{and}\left(iii\right)$ we get

For $x = 1 ⇒ y = 1 ⇒ {z}_{2} = 1 + i$ and for $x = \dfrac{1}{2 - \sqrt{2}} ⇒ y = \sqrt{2} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} ⇒ {z}_{1} = \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + \dfrac{i}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ {\left|\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 1\right)\sqrt{2} + i - \left(1 + i\right)\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left|\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|}^{2} = {\left|1 + \sqrt{2} + i - \left(1 + i\right)\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left|\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|}^{2} = {\left(\sqrt{2}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left|\sqrt{2}{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|}^{2} = 2$

questions.q: Consider the matrices : $A=\left[\begin{array}{ll}2 & -5 \\ 3 & m\end{array}\right], B=\left[\begin{array}{l}20 \\ m\end{array}\right]$ and $X=\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\ y\end{array}\right]$. Let the set of all $m$, for which the system of equations $A X=B$ has a negative solution (i.e., $x < 0$ and $y < 0$ ), be the interval $(a, b)$. Then $8 \int_a^b|A| d m$ is equal to_________
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & A=\left(\begin{array}{cc}2 & -5 \\ 3 & m\end{array}\right), B=\left(\begin{array}{c}20 \\ m\end{array}\right) \\ & X=\left(\begin{array}{l}x \\ y\end{array}\right) \\ & 2 x-5 y=20 \ldots(1)\\ & 3 x+m y=m \ldots(2)\\ & \Rightarrow y=\frac{2 m-60}{2 m+15} \\ & y < 0 \Rightarrow m \in\left(\frac{-15}{2}, 30\right)\end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}=\frac{25 \mathrm{~m}}{2 \mathrm{~m}+15} \\ & \mathrm{x} < 0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{m} \in\left(\frac{-15}{2}, 0\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{m} \in\left(\frac{-15}{2}, 0\right) \\ & |\mathrm{A}|=2 \mathrm{~m}+15 \end{aligned}$
Now, $\begin{aligned} & 8 \int_{\frac{-15}{2}}^0(2 \mathrm{~m}+15) \mathrm{dm}=8\left\{\mathrm{~m}^2+15 \mathrm{~m}\right\}_{\frac{-15}{2}}^0 \\ & \Rightarrow 8\left\{-\left(\frac{225}{4}-\frac{225}{2}\right)\right\} \\ & =8 \times \frac{225}{4}=450 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $A$ be a $2 \times 2$ real matrix and $I$ be the identity matrix of order $2 .$ If the roots of the equation $| A - xI | = 0$ be $- 1$ and $3,$ then the sum of the diagonal elements of the matrix ${A}^{2}$ is _____.
questions.solution:
Given: $| A - xI | = 0$ have roots $- 1$ and $3$.

Let, $A = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ A - xI = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right] - \left[\begin{cases}x & 0 \\ 0 & x\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ A - xI = \left[\begin{cases}a - x & b \\ c & d - x\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left|A - xI\right| = \left(a - x\right)\left(d - x\right) - bc$

$⇒ \left|A - xI\right| = ad - ax - dx + {x}^{2} - bc$

$⇒ \left|A - xI\right| = {x}^{2} - \left(a + d\right)x + \left(ad - bc\right)$

Sum of roots, $a + d = 2$

Product of roots, $ad - bc = - 3$

Now finding matrix ${A}^{2}$,

$⇒ {A}^{2} = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right] \times \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ {A}^{2} = \left[\begin{cases}{a}^{2} + bc & ab + bd \\ ac + cd & bc + {d}^{2}\end{cases}\right]$

Sum of diagonal elements, $S = {a}^{2} + bc + bc + {d}^{2}$

$⇒ S = {a}^{2} + 2bc + {d}^{2}$

$⇒ S = ( a + d{)}^{2} - 2\left(ad - bc\right)$

$⇒ S = ( 2{)}^{2} - 2\left(- 3\right)$

$⇒ S = 4 + 6$

$⇒ S = 10$

questions.q: Let $A = {I}_{2} - 2M{M}^{T},$ where $M$ is real matrix of order $2 \times 1$ such that the relation ${M}^{T}M = {I}_{1}$ holds. If $\lambda$ is a real number such that the relation $AX = \lambdaX$ holds for some non-zero real matrix $X$ of order $2 \times 1,$ then the sum of squares of all possible values of $\lambda$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given: $A = {I}_{2} - 2M{M}^{T}$

$⇒ {A}^{2} = \left({I}_{2} - 2M{M}^{T}\right)\left({I}_{2} - 2M{M}^{T}\right)$

$⇒ {A}^{2} = {I}_{2} - 2M{M}^{T} - 2M{M}^{T} + 4M{M}^{T}M{M}^{T}$

$⇒ {A}^{2} = {I}_{2} - 4M{M}^{T} + 4M{M}^{T}$ $\left\{\text{as}{M}^{T}M = {I}_{1}\right\}$

$⇒ {A}^{2} = {I}_{2}$

Also, $AX = \lambdaX$

$⇒ {A}^{2}X = \lambdaAX$

$⇒ X = \lambda\left(\lambdaX\right)$ $\left\{\text{as}{A}^{2} = {I}_{2} \text{ and } AX = \lambdaX\right\}$

$⇒ X = {\lambda}^{2}X$

$⇒ X\left({\lambda}^{2} - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ {\lambda}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ \lambda = \pm 1$

So, sum of square of all possible values $= 2$

If $\lambda$ is a real number such that the relation $AX = \lambdaX$ holds for some non-zero real matrix $X$ of order $2 \times 1,$ then the sum of squares of all possible values of $\lambda$ is equal to:
questions.explanation:
Given: $A = {I}_{2} - 2M{M}^{T}$

$⇒ {A}^{2} = \left({I}_{2} - 2M{M}^{T}\right)\left({I}_{2} - 2M{M}^{T}\right)$

$⇒ {A}^{2} = {I}_{2} - 2M{M}^{T} - 2M{M}^{T} + 4M{M}^{T}M{M}^{T}$

$⇒ {A}^{2} = {I}_{2} - 4M{M}^{T} + 4M{M}^{T}$ $\left\{\text{as}{M}^{T}M = {I}_{1}\right\}$

$⇒ {A}^{2} = {I}_{2}$

Also, $AX = \lambdaX$

$⇒ {A}^{2}X = \lambdaAX$

$⇒ X = \lambda\left(\lambdaX\right)$ $\left\{\text{as}{A}^{2} = {I}_{2} \text{ and } AX = \lambdaX\right\}$

$⇒ X = {\lambda}^{2}X$

$⇒ X\left({\lambda}^{2} - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ {\lambda}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ \lambda = \pm 1$

So, sum of square of all possible values $= 2$

questions.q: The number of ways in which $21$ identical apples can be distributed among three children such that each child gets at least $2$ apples, is
questions.solution:
Let us initially distribute $2$ apples to each children.

So, the remaining $15$ apples are to be distributed such that each children can get any number of apples.

So, the required number of ways will be given by $N = Cr - 1 n + r - 1$.

$⇒ N = C2 15 + 3 - 1$

$⇒ N = C2 17$

$⇒ N = \dfrac{17 \times 16}{2}$

$⇒ N = 136$

$⇒ N = 101$

$\begin{aligned} & P(W)=\frac{1}{3} \quad P(L)=\frac{2}{3} \\ & x=\text { number of matches that team wins } \\ & y=\text { number of matches that team loses } \\ & |x-y| \leq 2 \text { and } x+y=10 \\ & |x-y|=0,1,2 \quad x, y \in N\end{aligned}$
Case-I
$\begin{aligned}
& -I:|x-y|=0 \Rightarrow x=y \\
& \because x+y=10 \Rightarrow x=5=y \\
& P(|x-y|=0)={ }^{10} C_5\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^5\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^5
\end{aligned}$

\hline 2 \mathrm{y}=9 & 2 \mathrm{y}=11 \\
\hline \text{Not possible} & \text{Not possible} \\
\hline
\end{array}$

$⇒ a = P ( X = 3 )$

We know that, ${S}_{\infty} = a + ar + {ar}^{2} + . . . \infty = \dfrac{a}{1 - r}$

$⇒ b = \dfrac{\dfrac{25}{216}}{1 - \dfrac{5}{6}}$

$⇒ P ( X \ge 6 ) = {\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)}^{5}$

questions.q: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of the equation $p{x}^{2} + qx - r = 0$, where $p \ne 0$. If $p, q$ and $r$ be the consecutive terms of a non-constant G.P and $\dfrac{1}{\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{\beta} = \dfrac{3}{4}$, then the value of ${\left(\alpha - \beta\right)}^{2}$ is:
questions.solution:
Given: $\alpha\text{and}\beta$ be the roots of equation $p{x}^{2} + qx - r = 0$

So, $\alpha + \beta = - \dfrac{q}{p}, \alpha\beta = - \dfrac{r}{p}$

It is given that, $\dfrac{1}{\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{\beta} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\alpha + \beta}{\alpha\beta} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{q}{r} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Now, $p, q, r$ are in GP

So, common ratio of this GP will be $\dfrac{q}{p} = \dfrac{r}{q} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ p{x}^{2} + qx - r = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + \dfrac{q}{p}x - \dfrac{r}{p} = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + \dfrac{4}{3}x - {\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ 9{x}^{2} + 12x - 16 = 0$

$⇒ {\left(\alpha - \beta\right)}^{2} = {\left(\alpha + \beta\right)}^{2} - 4\alpha\beta$

$⇒ {\left(\alpha - \beta\right)}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{- 12}{9}\right)}^{2} - 4\left(\dfrac{- 16}{9}\right)$

$⇒ {\left(\alpha - \beta\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{16}{9} + \dfrac{64}{9}$

$⇒ {\left(\alpha - \beta\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{80}{9}$

questions.q: The number of solutions, of the equation ${e}^{sinx} - 2{e}^{- sinx} = 2$ is
questions.solution:
Let, ${e}^{sinx} = t$

$⇒ t - \dfrac{2}{t} = 2$

$⇒ {t}^{2} - 2t - 2 = 0$

$⇒ {t}^{2} - 2t + 1 = 3$

$⇒ {\left(t - 1\right)}^{2} = 3$

$⇒ t = 1 \pm \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ t \approx 2 . 73, - 0 . 73\left(\text{not possible}\right)$

$⇒ t \approx 2 . 73$

$⇒ {e}^{sinx} \approx 2 . 73$

$⇒ sinx \approx {\log}_{e}\left(2 . 73\right)$

$⇒ sinx > 1 \to \text{Not possible}$

So no solutions will be possible for the given equation.

questions.q: A software company sets up $m$ number of computer systems to finish an assignment in 17 days. If 4 computer systems crashed on the start of the second day, 4 more computer systems crashed on the start of the third day and so on, then it took 8 more days to finish the assignment. questions.q: If three successive terms of a G.P. with common ratio $r\left(r > 1\right)$ are the length of the sides of a triangle and $\left[r\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to r, then $3\left[r\right] + \left[- r\right]$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let, $a, ar, a{r}^{2} \to G . P .$

It is given that sum of any two sides is greater than the third side.

$⇒ a + ar > a{r}^{2}, a + a{r}^{2} > ar, ar + a{r}^{2} > a$

Case-I: ${r}^{2} - r - 1 < 0$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{1 - 4 \times 1 \times \left(- 1\right)}}{2}$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$

$⇒ r \in \left(\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{5}}{2}, \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\right) . . . \left(i\right)$

Case-II: ${r}^{2} - r + 1 > 0$ is always true.

Case-III: ${r}^{2} + r - 1 > 0$

$⇒ r \in \left(- \infty, \dfrac{- 1 - \sqrt{5}}{2}\right) ∪ \left(\dfrac{- 1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}, \infty\right) . . . \left(ii\right)$

Taking intersection of $\left(i\right)\text{and}\left(ii\right)$

$⇒ r \in \left(\dfrac{- 1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}, \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\right)$

As $r > 1$

$⇒ r \in \left(1, \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \left[r\right] = 1\text{and}\left[- r\right] = - 2$

$⇒ 3\left[r\right] + \left[- r\right] = 3 - 2$

$⇒ 3\left[r\right] + \left[- r\right] = 1$

If the mean of the following probability distribution of a random variable $\mathrm{X}$ :
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline \mathrm{X} & 0 & 2 & 4 & 6 & 8 \\
\hline \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X}) & a & 2 a & a+b & 2 b & 3 b \\
\hline
\end{array}$
is $\frac{46}{9}$, then the variance of the distribution is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \sum P_i=1 \\ & a+2 a+a+b+2 b+3 b=1\end{aligned}$ $4 a+6 b=1$ ...(I) $\mathrm{E}(\mathrm{x})=$ mean $=\frac{46}{9}$ $\begin{aligned} & \sum P_i X_i=\frac{46}{9} \Rightarrow 4 a+4 a+4 b+12 b+24 b=\frac{46}{9} \\ & 8 a+40 b=\frac{46}{9}\end{aligned}$ $4 a+20 b=\frac{23}{9}$ ...(II) Subtract (I) from (II) we get $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{b}=\frac{1}{9} \& \mathrm{a}=\frac{1}{12} \\ & \text { Variance }=\mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}{ }^2\right)-\mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)^2 \\ & \mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)^2=0^2 \times 9^2+2^2 \times 2 \mathrm{a}+4^2(\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b})+6^2(2 \mathrm{~b})+8^2(3 \mathrm{~b}) \\ & =24 \mathrm{a}+280 \mathrm{~b} \end{aligned}$
Put $\mathrm{a}=\frac{1}{12} \quad \mathrm{~b}=\frac{1}{9}$ $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^2\right)=2+\frac{280}{9}=\frac{298}{9} \\ & \therefore \sigma^2=\mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^2\right)-\mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)^2 \\ & =\frac{298}{9}-\left(\frac{46}{9}\right)^2 \\ & \sigma^2=\frac{298}{9}-\frac{2116}{81} \\ & =\frac{566}{81} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: From a lot of 10 items, which include 3 defective items, a sample of 5 items is drawn at random. Let the random variable $\mathrm{X}$ denote the number of defective items in the sample. If the variance of $\mathrm{X}$ is $\sigma^2$, then $96 \sigma^2$ is equal to ______
questions.solution:
$X=$ denotes number of defective
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline \mathrm{x} & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\
\hline \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{x}) & \frac{7}{15} & \frac{5}{12} & \frac{5}{12} & \frac{1}{12} \\
\hline \mathrm{x}_1{ }^2 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 9 \\
\hline \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}} \mathrm{x}_1{ }^2 & 0 & \frac{5}{12} & \frac{20}{12} & \frac{9}{12} \\
\hline \mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{i}} \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}} & 0 & \frac{5}{12} & \frac{10}{12} & \frac{3}{12} \\
\hline
\end{array}$
$\mu=\Sigma \mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{i}} \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}=\frac{18}{12}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \Sigma \mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{i}} \mathrm{x}_1^2=\frac{34}{12} \\
& \sigma^2=\Sigma \mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{i}} \mathrm{x}_1^2-(\mu)^2
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{34}{12}-\left(\frac{18}{12}\right)^2=\frac{17}{6}-\frac{9}{4} \\ & \frac{34-27}{12}=\frac{7}{12} \\ & 96 \sigma^2=96 \times \frac{7}{12}=56\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c} \in \mathrm{N}$ and $\mathrm{a} < \mathrm{b} < \mathrm{c}$. Let the mean, the mean deviation about the mean and the variance of the 5 observations $9,25, \mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}$ be 18,4 and $\frac{136}{5}$, respectively. Then $2 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}-\mathrm{c}$ is equal to__________
questions.solution:
$a, b, c \in N \quad a < b < c$
$\overline{\mathrm{x}}=$ mean $=\frac{9+25+\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c}}{5}=18$
$a+b+c=56$
Mean deviation $=\frac{\Sigma\left|\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}-\overline{\mathrm{x}}\right|}{\mathrm{n}}=4$
$\begin{aligned} & =9+7+|18-\mathrm{a}|+|18-\mathrm{b}|+|18-\mathrm{c}|=20 \\ & =|18-\mathrm{a}|+|18-\mathrm{b}|+|18-\mathrm{c}|=4\end{aligned}$
Variance $=\frac{\Sigma\left|\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}-\overline{\mathrm{x}}\right|^2}{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{136}{5}$
$\begin{aligned} & =81+49+|18-a|^2+|18-b|^2+|18-c|^2=136 \\ & =(18-a)^2+(18-b)^2+(18-c)^2=6\end{aligned}$
Possible values $(18-\mathrm{a})^2=1, \quad(18-\mathrm{b})^2=1 \quad(18-\mathrm{c})^2=4$ $\mathrm{a} < \mathrm{b} < \mathrm{c}$
so $\quad \begin{array}{ccc}18-a=1 & 18-b=-1 & 18-c=-2 \\ \mathrm{a}=17 & \mathrm{~b}=19 & \mathrm{c}=20\end{array}$
$a+b+c=56$
$2 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}-\mathrm{c} 34=19-20=33$

questions.q: The mean and standard deviation of $15$ observations were found to be $12$ and $3$ respectively. On rechecking it was found that an observation was read as $10$ in place of $12 .$ If $\mu$ and ${\sigma}^{2}$ denote the mean and variance of the correct observations respectively, then $15\left(\mu + {\mu}^{2} + {\sigma}^{2}\right)$ is equal to _________.
questions.solution:
Given: Incorrect mean, $x = 12$ and incorrect standard deviation, ${\sigma}^{'} = 3$.

$⇒ \dfrac{{Σx}_{i}}{15} = 12$

$⇒ {Σx}_{i} = 180$

Correct mean is given by,

$\mu = \dfrac{{Σx}_{i} - 10 + 12}{15}$

$⇒ \mu = \dfrac{182}{15}$

Also, ${\sigma}^{'} = \sqrt{\dfrac{∑ {x}_{i}^{2}}{15} - 144} = 3$

$⇒ \dfrac{∑ {x}_{i}^{2}}{15} = 9 + 144$

$⇒ ∑ {x}_{i}^{2} = 2295$

Correct ${Σx}_{i}^{2} = 2295 - 100 + 144 = 2339$

${\sigma}^{2}$ (correct variance) $= \dfrac{2339}{15} - \dfrac{182 \times 182}{15 \times 15}$

$⇒ 15\left(\mu + {\mu}^{2} + {\sigma}^{2}\right) = 15\left(\dfrac{182}{15} + \dfrac{182 \times 182}{15 \times 15} + \dfrac{2339}{15} - \dfrac{182 \times 182}{15 \times 15}\right)$

$⇒ 15\left(\mu + {\mu}^{2} + {\sigma}^{2}\right) = 15\left(\dfrac{182}{15} + \dfrac{2339}{15}\right)$

$⇒ 15\left(\mu + {\mu}^{2} + {\sigma}^{2}\right) = 2521$
